title: Ampleness of an already constructed admissible finite group quotient
statement: Let V be a Noetherian scheme [pqf-def-locnoeth], H a finite group acting by scheme automorphisms a on V, and q:V→Q a morphism of schemes satisfying IsAdmissibleFiniteSchemeQuotient a q [def-per-admissible-finite-scheme-quotient]. Given an absolutely ample invertible module L on V [def-sc-invertible-module, def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module], there exists an absolutely ample invertible module M on the given scheme Q. No quotient is constructed, no relative immersion is asserted, and no properness, normality, free action or characteristic hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Original lem-per-projective-finite-group-quotient Steps 8--9; Rydh arXiv:0708.3333v2 Proposition 4.7, norm argument (read online; WANTED locally); Stacks Properties 09NV, 01PV, 01PS.

proof.text: Form N=the tensor product over h∈H of a_h^*L with permutation linearization. Apply orbit_tensor_line_descent to the invariant-section formula in hq. Its formulas expressed on equal inverse-image opens are equivalent to the overlap equations in hq: restrict the equation on the whole invariant open to any common subopen, and conversely take that whole open. This supplies an invertible M on Q, the isomorphism q^*M≅N and fixed sections for every tensor power. The fixed-section inclusion specifies M uniquely as a subsheaf.

source.place: Rydh Theorem 4.4 and Proposition 4.7; original quotient steps 8--9

proof.text: For y∈Q its inverse image E is a finite orbit, by finiteness, surjectivity and the orbit-fibre clause of hq. Choose a positive-power section s of L with affine nonvanishing locus containing E, using the ample finite-set lemma. Tensor all a_h^*s. The tensor comparison identifies it as a section σ of N^d, fixed by the permutation linearization, so descent gives t in Γ(Q,M^d).

source.place: Rydh Theorem 4.4 and Proposition 4.7; original quotient steps 8--9

proof.text: The pullback and tensor fibre formulas identify V_σ with the intersection of the finitely many inverse images of V_s. It contains E. Begin with the identity factor V_s and successively apply affine_cap_section_open to the other section factors. Thus this invariant intersection is affine.

source.place: Rydh Theorem 4.4 and Proposition 4.7; original quotient steps 8--9

proof.text: The fibre formula and q^*M≅N give q^-1(Q_t)=V_σ. An invariant affine open Spec A in an admissible quotient has affine image Spec A^H: the orbit topology identifies their spaces, and the sectionwise invariant formula identifies their sheaves by C_f=(A_f)^H, proved by a common annihilating power for the finitely many differences h(a)-a. This works with zero divisors. Therefore Q_t is affine and contains y.

source.place: Rydh Theorem 4.4 and Proposition 4.7; original quotient steps 8--9

proof.text: Q is quasi-compact, as the continuous surjective image of V, which is quasi-compact by ampleness. The sections t through each point are exactly the remaining clause of the absolute ample criterion, proving M ample.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_ample_on_admissible_finiteGroup_quotient
    {V Q : Scheme.{u}} [IsNoetherian V]
    (H : Type v) [Group H] [Finite H] (a : H →* Aut V) (q : V ⟶ Q)
    (hq : IsAdmissibleFiniteSchemeQuotient a q)
    (L : V.Modules) [L.IsInvertible] (hL : Scheme.Modules.IsAmple V L) :
    ∃ (M : Q.Modules) (hM : M.IsInvertible), @Scheme.Modules.IsAmple Q M hM
